title: Customers report outages at Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo
html:
• Published

Thousands of customers at major US banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, have reported trouble accessing services.

Chase Bank - the largest banking institution in the US - said a "software bug" in its hardware systems may have been behind the glitch and noted the impacts may have affected other banks. It added the issue was "temporary" and not "systemic" or "cyber-related".

Problems appeared to be easing for many customers by early Monday evening.

The issue comes after a string of unrelated technical problems last week, including a massive Microsoft outage, as well as a telecommunications issue and network failure that grounded all US flights.

Problems started throughout the afternoon on Monday. There were almost 5,000 reports of Chase Bank's services being down, according to the Downdetector website.

Chase Bank told it's customers that "some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete" but they still had "access to their accounts and funds".

The bank, a subsidiary of JP Morgan Chase, serves more than 86m customers at 5,000 branches across the US, as well as 7.4m small businesses, according to the company's webpage. It is also the top credit card issuer in the US.

The exact nature of the bug was unclear. The BBC has contacted Chase Bank.

Another institution, US Bank, said some its systems were not directly affected but clients using the Zelle, a digital payment platform, received error messages saying their payments could not be sent.

Zelle has said its service is "operating as it should" and issues at other banks could be affecting payments.

Customers also reported issues with Truist, PNC and Capital One but all these companies told the BBC they have not been impacted.

As of 1800 ET (2300G), Chase, Bank of America and US Bank had seen a fall in the number of reported outages.
summary: Chase Bank, the largest US bank, said a software bug might be causing the issue, but that it was not "systemic'" or "cyber-related".
